newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee promotes executives, succession seen.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee promotes executives, succession seen.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp. Thursday appointed a president and a vice chairman in moves analysts said were to lay the groundwork for a successor to Chairman John Bryan.
The food and consumer products company appointed C. Steven McMillan to the position of president and Donald Franceschini to the position of vice chairman, effective immediately.
Both McMillan and Franceschini report to Bryan and serve on the company's board of directors, the company said in a statement.
"These promotions represent our desire to begin an orderly transition -- for both the short-term and long-term management of Sara Lee Corp.," Bryan said in a statement.
Bryan, 60, has been chairman of Sara Lee since 1976. He has hinted that McMillan, 50, could succeed him one day as head of the company.

McMillan was executive vice president of Sara Lee's Meats and Bakery, Coffee and Grocery, and Household and Body Care lines of business, and Franceschini was executive vice president of the Personal Products business.
Bryan has been chairman since 1976, the same year that McMillan joined the company.
"Both have good track records and both are held in high regard," said Ellen Baras, an analyst at Nesbitt Burns.

"McMillan is clearly being tested," she added. "Looking at the two of them, McMillan is age-appropriate for the appointment (to succeed Bryan). He'll also be involved in all aspects of Sara Lee's businesses," Baras said.
"They've been right below Bryan for some time now, and they've both done incredible jobs for Sara Lee," said Sally Schaadt, an analyst at Fourteen Research.

Sara Lee spokeswoman Theresa Herlevsen told Reuters that Bryan has said he would retire in the autumn of 2001 at the age of 65, while Franceschini, 61, planned to retire in the autumn of 1998. Sara Lee does not have a mandatory retirement age, but most executives retire at age 62 or 63, she said.
Herlevsen said the company eventually planned to name the 50-year-old McMillan to the additional post of chief opertating officer.

"Each of these individuals has demonstrated exceptional leadership and management capabilities. Their promotions today reflect my confidence in the management team that will join me in leading Sara Lee Corporation into the next century," Bryan said.
The post of president at Sara Lee had been vacant for about three years since the resignation of Cornelias Boonstra, an executive from one of the company's European subsidiaries.
McMillan has shone as the executive in charge of Sara Lee's expanding meats, bakery and body care product lines. "All these businesses have performed very well," Herlevsen said.
McMillan will continue with his current operating responsibilities and will be involved in the strategic direction of all of the corporation's businesses, including Personal Products.

The company's board of directors also promoted Senior Vice President Frank Meysman to the post of executive vice president. Meysman, based in Utrecht, the Netherlands, serves as chairman of the Board of Management of Sara Lee/DE. He will report to McMillan.
Sara Lee's stock fell 62.5 cents to $42.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
